items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: this was part of the Ham Crawford band because we changed personnel. And this was Brooks Pruitt and Dick Coleman and Buddy Seaton and myself

ctx.x: Well, this is a band that plays stocks. Uh-huh. Oh, yeah. Yeah, I told you about them. Yes. And they try to bring back every detail directly. Which is nice that they're doing that. And it's marvelous to see things done that way. Anyway, uh, you told me about some band that you went to Lake Charles with.

Well, this was part of the Ham Crawford band because we changed personnel. And this was Brooks Pruitt and Dick Coleman and Buddy Seaton and myself and a boy from Software, Louisiana, named Alvin Tonietta, who was a local guy who played trumpet. But now, I was going to tell you about some men who played with Ham Crawford earlier, I mean later. Dick, he went to San Antonio and did the usual thing of reorganizing a band to take out on the road and it was easy to get guys to go. Among these people that he is was…

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: who included Red Roundtree and Buddy Seaton on drums and Shockey Wilcox on trumpet. And Red Roundtree was a very famous banjo player... So the Buddies then, after the Buddies broke up...

ctx.x: I didn't get what he played. Well, actually, this was just a little trio.

And, it was Jack and Terry Sheehan up in, uh, Thomas John, and William Gramsson, and all that stuff. And, they played all the society dances, and they played the Fiori roof garden. And, this particular man, this guy, who I was talking about, uh, was, uh, Asian. He hired them. And, uh, so I guess the buddies then, uh, who, uh, who, uh, were, uh, uh, who, uh, were included the Red Round Tree and Buddy Seeky and drums and, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um,…
No, that's right. You didn't tell me much about New Orleans, you tripped down.
